svg.title: Apply flow: from pull request to dispatch
svg.desc: On a pull request, validate-and-plan.yml runs four jobs: maintenance-tests, rebuild-policy-tests, validate-and-plan on the self-hosted runner, and comment, which posts the plan as a sticky comment. The plan job saves plan.tfplan and plan.exitcode to an S3 bucket under pr-n. A person merges the pull request. apply.yml then runs check-conditions, which stops on a skip pattern and reads the mode from the pull request body: normal applies the saved plan; drain needs the confirm box and cordons and drains every node before applying the saved plan; destroy needs the confirm box and runs terraform destroy followed by a fresh apply. The apply job runs scripts/maintenance_apply.py under the maintenance lock: acquire, applying, recovering, release, with ownership verified before every command. A failed command keeps the lock. If something changed, trigger-ansible sends the repository dispatch infrastructure-changed with the payload drained_nodes to ansible's deploy.yml, and cleanup deletes the saved plan. Separately, drift.yml plans every day at 08:00 UTC and opens, comments on or closes an issue labelled drift.
svg.text: after the merge, or started by hand

g.text: stops on a skip pattern such as [skip ci],
then reads the mode from the checkboxes in the PR body
If a command fails, the lock stays held and no dispatch is sent. A person has to release it.

svg.text: deletes pr-<n>/ from the bucket after a saved-plan run
daily at 08:00 UTC, or by hand

g.text: opened when a plan finds drift
closed when the plan is clean

svg.text: Started by hand, apply.yml has no saved plan: it runs terraform apply -auto-approve and always dispatches.
